viz_reviews.summary: Both examples render the framework's native shape: a throughput band on top and a textbook Evaporating Cloud below with A/B/C/D/D' guide letters. Provenance is the strongest dimension - facts-only collapses the TBPN cloud to 14 nodes and 3 edges, an honest demonstration that the cloud's structure is nearly all LLM-supplied. Stats, grounding toggle and panel match graph.json exactly; metrics clean in every view. Remaining issues are positional polish only.

notes: Research: Goldratt, The Goal (1984) and It's Not Luck (1994). TOC's five focusing steps (identify, exploit, subordinate, elevate, repeat) treat throughput as set by one constraint; the Evaporating Cloud (conflict resolution diagram) is one of the five Thinking Processes trees, laid out as A (objective) <- B, C (requirements) <- D, D' (prerequisites), with D and D' in conflict. The cloud's leverage is that the B-D and C-D' arrows rest on unstated assumptions; surfacing them and invalidating one (the injection) evaporates the conflict rather than compromising. Eight slots: goal/step/constraint carry the throughput view, objective/requirement/prerequisite/assumption/injection carry the cloud. Decision: assumption nodes are always derived (never stated by speakers), injection carries the idea field. | Scout returned three candidates: (1) CoreWeave/Brian Venturo 2025-07-15, (2) Groq/Jonathan Ross 2025-07-08 (HBM as the bottleneck), (3) AI capex wall 2025-10-23 (fabs vs energy). Chose (1): it is the only one where the SAME speaker names the binding constraint, eliminates the popular candidates with evidence, and then states the chronic conflict that constraint produces - so the cloud is about the constraint, which is the case the Evaporating Cloud exists for. (2) was strong but its injection is stated in the source (Groq removed the memory), which would leave the injection slot a fact and lose the framework's payoff; (3) is hosts reading an essay aloud, so the conflict is reported, not owned. | Decision: the constraint node c1 is a FACT here, against the registry's typical_provenance 'derived', because Venturo names it outright ('the biggest constraint is speculative capital'). The derived work moves to c2 (where the constraint goes next) and to the four assumptions. | Decision: four assumptions per example rather than five - the objective-to-requirement arrow on the survival side (a bankrupt company serves nobody) is trivially valid and adds a node without adding insight; it is noted in the README instead. | Decision: no idea field on the classic example, so the gold ring reads unambiguously as 'this is where the opportunity is' in the TBPN example only. | Only 3 of 29 TBPN edges are facts (el3, el4, ec2) against 7 of 20 in the classic. That is the example's real lesson, not a defect: written scenario prose states its own connectives ('to keep cost per part down he is expected to...'), diarised speech almost never does, so in a transcript the cloud's arrows are all inference. | Resume: the first framework-agent process was killed after the README child wrote README.md but before it was committed. The resuming agent verified the untracked README field by field against graph.json (every node and edge id cited, texts, labels, quotes, rationales, confidences and idea fields identical; all headings match the SPEC 6 template; all five relative links resolve) and kept it rather than relaunching a README child. | Viz loop passed on iteration 1 (demonstrates 4, provenance 5, legibility 4, fidelity 5, no blocking issues). The critic's seven suggestions were left unapplied because the protocol stops the loop on a pass and re-editing layout after a passing verdict would ship an artifact no critic has seen; they are recorded in viz_reviews[0].suggestions for the wave review. Two engine-level observations from the builder that the orchestrator may want to act on for all frameworks: (a) the layout object has no free-text annotation primitive, so the cloud's A/B/C/D/D' letters are drawn as near-degenerate guides whose line is invisible and only the label shows - an `annotations: [{pos, text}]` field would be the honest primitive; (b) snap.mjs metrics() measures only .nlabel, so edge labels (.elabel) are not in the overlap count and a page can score zero overlaps while an edge label sits on a node label - this example carries 8 labelled edges. | Reconcile: README bold labels updated to the viz builder's six shortened labels (cg1, g1, g2, s_ups, s_fiber, c2); everything else in the README already matched graph.json exactly. graph.json content (layout, node layout fields and labels stripped) is byte-identical to the scaffold commit. The rebuild at reconcile picked up an updated _meta/graph-engine.html that anchors each node label below the glyph the node actually draws, which resolves five of the critic's seven positional suggestions; re-ran snap after it and both examples still report 0 overlapping pairs, 0 off-screen, 0 under cards, clean console. One critic suggestion was tried and reverted: moving cc1/cc2 to sit under cs2/cs3 fixed the semantic misread (cc2 sitting under 'Assembly and shipping') but pushed the 'sets the rate' edge label onto the cs4 node label, which is a collision snap.mjs does not measure; the builder's positions are the better trade and were restored byte-identical. | Polish after snap.mjs metrics grew stricter (edge labels and decor captions now measured): TBPN went from 3 overlapping pairs to 0 by lifting b1/d1 to y=-2 (moves the 'invalid under offtake' midpoint label out from under d1's label), a1 to y=-9, the inj1/inj2/a4 column to x=48 with inj1 at y=-11, o1 to x=-44 with guide A to x=-52 (clears the C letter); classic went from 1 to 0 by moving ci1 to x=50. Layout fields only, no edge label text changed.
